title: Mobile runtime evidence and simulator CI
objective: Expose validated loopback/isolation/worker evidence in runtime.ready and physical-device receipts, and continuously compile exact-asset iPhone and iPad simulator builds on macOS

oracles: Bridge protocol, receipt validator, fixtures, and workflow contract tests

handoff.summary: runtime.ready now carries a strictly validated, capability-free observation of the loopback HTTP origin, cross-origin isolation, SharedArrayBuffer availability, and the outer/nested module-worker topology. The physical-device receipt schema and validator require the same evidence for a passing receipt and preserve honest unobserved fields for blocked fixtures. A macOS CI workflow builds the exact production-attested mobile asset closure for installed iPhone and iPad simulator destinations and uploads an artifact-identity-bound build receipt and logs.
risks: The macOS simulator workflow cannot run on this Linux lane; its exact-asset preparation, destination selection, two Release xcodebuild invocations, and receipt fields are protected by a static contract test and must receive an actual GitHub Actions receipt after integration.
No signed physical iPhone/iPad or TestFlight account was available. The checked-in fixtures remain explicitly blocked and must not be presented as device evidence.

The focused mobile checks pass. The broad portable check initially failed because this fresh worktree had no generated dist tree; its subsequent full build was stopped at the parent's immediate-integration request. Native and SEA were therefore not rerun for this TypeScript/JSON/workflow-only follow-up; the integration lane should use its current receipts and rerun them at the release checkpoint.
next_steps: Run the mobile-simulators workflow after integration and retain its uploaded sagejs.mobile-simulator-build/v1 receipt for both form factors.

Replace each blocked fixture only after capturing runtime.ready and completing all checks on a signed physical iPhone and iPad; then submit the same artifact through TestFlight and update its status honestly.
